widgetData.content:
Stockport County Women climbed into third place in the FAWNL Division One North on Sunday with a thumping 4-0 win away at York City Ladies.

Tash Tezgel's side made it nine games unbeaten in all competitions with a dominant display on the road, leading after just seven minutes when Chloe Fisher fired home her first goal for the club. Imogen Porteous-Williams doubled the advantage before the break, with Katie Anderson and Porteous-Williams adding further goals in the second half to seal a resounding victory for the Hatters.

County made four changes to the side that beat Chesterfield in the FAWNL Cup the previous weekend, with Fisher coming in for her first league start for the club up front, following her summer move from Liverpool Feds.

Ruby Scott, Ellie Fletcher and Monika Stube also started for Tezgel's side, with Meg Parker, Maddie Robinson, Meg Boydell and Em Bradshaw dropping to the bench.

County were up and running in next to no time in Yorkshire, as Ellie Fletcher broke clear down the right flank in the seventh minute, with her ball in running through for Fisher to finish hard and low for her maiden Hatters goal.

York City almost responded immediately as Ella Martin fired an effort just over the crossbar, but then came a moment of controversy on 25 minutes as Ellie Fletcher broke clear of the York backline before being hauled down by a defender. Despite strong appeals for a red card from the travelling County supporters, the referee opted to show just a yellow.

It mattered little in any event for the Hatters, who doubled their lead just past the half-hour mark. Katie Anderson was the provider from midfield, sliding the ball through to Porteous-Williams, who beat the offside trap and fired home via the inside of the post for her sixth league goal of the campaign.

It could have been three for County before the break, with Fisher steering Fletcher's cut-back narrowly over the crossbar, but the Hatters went in at the break in a commanding position.

Half-Time: York City Ladies 0-2 County Women (Fisher, 7'; Porteous-Williams, 31').

The second half took a while to get going, although County remained in control throughout. Substitute Em Bradshaw then sparked the game into life on 67 minutes with a sensational solo run, taking on three York City players before seeing her effort well saved by goalkeeper Wallace.

The third goal came just a few minutes later, with Bradshaw releasing Livvi Turkington down the left, and her cross was headed home emphatically by Anderson for her second goal in as many games.

Three quickly became four for the Hatters, thanks to a moment of real quality from Porteous-Williams. Found in space 25 yards from goal, the forward looked up and hit a stunning effort into the top corner for her second of the game.

Yaz Ahmed was denied a fifth for County late on after seeing her back-post header well-saved, but County were still able to celebrate a third straight league success.

Momentum is gathering for Tash Tezgel's side, who climbed above Halifax and into the top three with Sunday's victory, sitting six points behind league leaders Leeds United.

For now, County's attention turns back to the Women's FA Cup, with the Hatters travelling to Boldmere St Michaels on Sunday 15th November for a second-round tie.

Full-Time: York City Ladies 0-4 County Women (Fisher, 7'; Porteous-Williams, 31' & 74'; Anderson, 71').

postTitle: Match Report: York City Ladies 0-4 County Women
